You check whether a knowledge-base article answers a support ticket for a clinical practice-management product. Set answers_ticket to true only if following the article would resolve what the ticket actually asks. An article about a related task does not answer it: an article on placing an order does not answer a question about cancelling one. If the ticket asks for more than one thing, the article must answer all of them: an article that covers only part of the request does not answer it. Give the reason in one sentence.

Reply with only a JSON object and no other text.
Output: grounding.
The JSON object must match this JSON schema:
{"additionalProperties": false, "description": "Whether the best-matching article actually answers the ticket.", "properties": {"answers_ticket": {"title": "Answers Ticket", "type": "boolean"}, "reason": {"minLength": 1, "title": "Reason", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["answers_ticket", "reason"], "title": "grounding", "type": "object"}

Article id: troubleshoot-lab-interface
Article: Troubleshoot lab interface connections and missing feeds
When electronic diagnostic results stop populating, clinic staff can resolve most interface disruptions using the administrative console.

### Steps to Restart the Feed
1. Navigate to **Admin > Interfaces > Lab Connectivity**.
2. Locate the affected vendor in the active connections list.
3. Click **Diagnostics** to run a live ping test.
4. If the status reads offline, click **Action > Restart Service**.
5. Wait three minutes for the queue to flush and refresh the dashboard.

### Limits and Conditions
Only users with the *System Administrator* role can restart interface services. The system processes up to 500 queued results per batch; backlog clearing for extended outages may take up to thirty minutes.

### Troubleshooting
If the connection status remains red after a manual restart, verify that your local firewall permits outbound traffic on port 443 to the designated gateway IP. Should results still fail to appear, document the error code displayed in the event log and submit a support ticket with the specimen requisition numbers for the missing labs.

Ticket:
Troubleshooting electronic lab requisition rejections

Good morning, I am working on getting our electronic lab ordering workflow sorted out across the practice, but I hit a roadblock with some rejected requisitions. When I navigate to the diagnostic orders tab and click into the failed transmission queue, the error codes just say generic failure without explaining why the ICD-10 codes or test panels were rejected by the reference lab. I tried updating the diagnosis pointers on a few test orders and resubmitting them, but they bounced back again instantly. Could you walk me through how to properly clear these out and successfully transmit them?
